title: Meringue mushrooms
subtitle: piped meringue caps and stalks for a Yule log or chocolate cake
excerpt: Meringue mushrooms are a piped decoration made from stiff meringue: caps and stalks are piped separately onto a lined tray, dried in a low oven, and joined with a little melted chocolate. The stalks press into the soft underside of the caps before the meringue fully sets, which gives a clean join once dry. A dusting of cocoa makes them look like real field mushrooms.
sourceNotes: Meringue mushroom decoration traditional on the French Buche de Noel from at least the early twentieth century, widely adopted in British Christmas baking from the 1960s onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: Egg whites beaten with sugar until the mixture holds a firm, upright peak that does not droop when the whisk is lifted. The stage needed for piped meringue shapes.

content.text: Meringue mushrooms are a piped decoration for a Yule log, chocolate cake, or celebration cake. The caps and stalks are piped separately from
, dried in a low oven, and joined with melted chocolate. A dusting of cocoa over the finished mushrooms completes the look.

For 12 to 14 mushrooms, beat 2 large egg whites to soft peak, then add 100 g caster sugar a tablespoon at a time, beating until the meringue is stiff and glossy. A round piping tip, about 1 cm diameter, gives the best shape for both caps and stalks.
Heat the oven to 100 C (fan 80 C / gas 1/4). Line a large baking tray with baking paper.

Fit the piping bag with a plain round nozzle. Pipe the caps: hold the bag vertically and press out a round mound about 3 cm in diameter. Release the pressure and flick the bag sideways to stop a pointed tip forming. If a tip forms, wet your finger and press it flat immediately.
Pipe the stalks on the same tray but with a gap between the two sets. Hold the bag upright and pipe a short cylinder about 2 cm tall and 1 cm wide. Taper it very slightly toward the top.
Pipe the same number of stalks as caps plus two or three spares, as some may break when you press them in.
Bake the caps and stalks for 1.5 hours until completely dry and crisp. They should lift cleanly from the paper and sound hollow when tapped. Leave to cool fully on the tray.
Melt 30 g dark chocolate in a small bowl. Use a skewer or the tip of a cocktail stick to make a small indent in the underside of each cap.

Dip the top of a stalk into the melted chocolate and push it into the indent on the underside of a cap. Hold for 30 seconds. Stand the assembled mushroom upright on a board and leave for 15 minutes until the chocolate sets.
Dust with cocoa powder through a fine sieve for the finished look.

attrs.problem: Meringue caps spreading flat rather than holding a round mound
attrs.avoid: Avoid under-beaten meringue; it will not hold its shape through piping.
attrs.fix: Beat to full stiff peak before piping. The meringue should not droop or fall when the bowl is turned upside down.

attrs.problem: Stalks breaking when pressed into the caps
attrs.avoid: Avoid applying heavy pressure when joining; the stalk is fragile once dry.
attrs.fix: Make a small indent in the cap underside first with a skewer, then use just the melted chocolate and light pressure to push the stalk in.

attrs.problem: Meringue soft and sticky after baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid opening the oven during the first hour of drying; the temperature drop causes the meringue to weep.
attrs.fix: Extend the baking time by 30 minutes and leave the meringues in the oven with the door ajar as the oven cools.
